title: But by Saint Patrick
html_source: This quick reference comes from the scene where Horatio reproves Hamlet: “These are but wild and whirling words, my Lord.” Hamlet responds: “I’m sorry they offend you…” Horatio: “There’s no offence, my Lord.” Hamlet: “Yes, by Saint Patrick, but there is.” Horatio: “And much offense, too.” This captures the essence of this entire chapter. There is much offence by Saint Patrick as symbol of Ireland, But there is much offence to Saint Patrick, as the spiritual symbol of Ireland.
